newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber dull on string of bearish reports.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber dull on string of bearish reports.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midday on Thursday as players sat on the sidelines due to a string of bearish reports going around the market, dealers said.

"People are still worried about the currency problems in the region. There is also talk that Thailand may sell the rubber it bought from its farmers while the GM strike added to the depressed picture. We would want a clearer view of how this would affect the market before going back in," a dealer said.
Southeast Asian currencies have been rocked for weeks by a wave of speculative attacks.
General Motors in the U.S. was hit by a walkout by workers at a key transmission and wheel plant in Warren, Michigan.
Major consumers were not seen asking for offers in the market although dealers were hopeful that some buying may emerge in the afternoon session.
Traders said Michelin, which was said to be engaged in its monthly buying programme, may be interested in picking up more rubber for nearby delivery.
At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 92.00-94.00 U.S. cents a kg from 92.00 cents.
